A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Off-CMAB framework and CLCB algorithms. The complete main texts, appendices, equations, table, and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and real-world experiments for cascading bandits and LLM caching in Section 5 and Appendix G, including Yelp and SciQ results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix J, including the additional GPT-4-turbo evaluation.

M1.justification: CLCB and its cascading-bandit, caching, influence-maximization, and online streaming variants retain the same procedures. The standard caching algorithm and influence-maximization algorithm are relocated and renumbered, not newly introduced or modified.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic cascading-bandit and caching tasks, Yelp recommendations, and SciQ-based caching. The additional offline-use examples in v2 Appendix B are motivation, not new evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain CUCB-Offline and EMP for cascading bandits, and LFU and LEC for caching. v2 expands baseline descriptions and cites additional related methods without evaluating new comparators.

E3.justification: The experimental settings remain unchanged, including item/query counts, recommendation and cache sizes, dataset-size sweeps, cost definitions, and GPT-4-o/GPT-4-turbo configurations. Appendix J preserves the settings documented in v1 Appendix G.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the four data-generation comparisons in Figure 2, action/cache-size comparisons, and the GPT-4-turbo check in Figure 4. No additional ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Both experimental appendices specify 20 independent trials and mean/standard-deviation reporting for synthetic caching. v2 repeats the trial count in the main text; this is neither a new disclosure nor evidence of additional runs.

E6.justification: The embedded plots underlying Figures 1–4 are identical, and their reported rankings and numerical findings are retained. These include the stated 47.75% and 20.02% cascading-gap reductions against CUCB-Offline and EMP.

T1.justification: v2 omits the paragraph in v1 Section 2.3 explicitly defining K* as the number of triggerable arms and stating the ordering of the three action-size measures. The two barred quantities remain defined in Theorem 1. The substantive theorem bounds and proof derivations otherwise match; the additional influence-maximization theorem repeats an existing result.

C1.justification: The central claims remain the first offline CMAB framework, pessimistic CLCB, two coverage conditions, near-optimal guarantees, and three applications. The new conclusion summarizes these existing contributions without changing their scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix B explains offline-only applicability through batched recommendation updates and outsourced caching design using private logs, and discusses future hybrid learning. Appendix A.1 adds an explanation of the informational distinction between full-bandit and arm-level feedback.

D1.justification: The experimental appendices retain the same data preparation, model encodings, sample counts, and hardware disclosure: macOS, Apple M3 Pro, and 18 GB RAM. No new implementation settings, code availability, or dataset-access instructions are provided.

R1.justification: v2 adds a focused discussion of full-bandit CMAB, citing Niazadeh, Nie, Fourati, and Sun, plus references supporting hybrid learning and application context. Several introductory learning-to-rank citations are removed. The principal positioning against offline RL and existing caching/influence-maximization work remains.

P1.justification: Related work moves from Section 1.1 to Appendix A; detailed influence maximization moves to Appendix C; and the bibliography moves before the appendices. v2 adds a motivation appendix, conclusion, acknowledgements, and impact statement, alongside condensed application introductions and revised cross-references.

P2.justification: The main text and bibliography change from a single-column preprint layout to a two-column conference layout. Figures 1–3 become substantially smaller column-width displays, Table 1 is reformatted, and algorithm boxes are relocated. The underlying plot content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The concrete offline-use rationale in Appendix B, expanded feedback-model positioning, and new conclusion provide a modest explanatory improvement while preserving the scientific evidence. The gain is limited by smaller main-text plots and omission of the explicit action-size definition paragraph; no stronger experimental or theoretical validation is added.
